summary: markSaved advances savedVersion monotonically and is guarded only by path, while openModel resets version/savedVersion to 0 on a SAME-PATH re-seed — so a save that resolves after a force re-seed stamps a pre-reseed version onto the new model, leaving savedVersion far above version and making isDirty() report CLEAN for the next N real edits.
silent_failure_scenario: Note N is open in tab T with model version=12, savedVersion=3. A save fails (OneDrive/Defender holds the .md), the save-health banner appears, and the 10s auto-retry timer (store.ts:1745-1751 → retrySaveFailure, store.ts:512) fires saveNoteSession, which composes version 12 synchronously and awaits a slow write. retrySaveFailure is NOT gated by isCascading/isReseeding. While that write is in flight the user clicks "Discard my changes" → discardFailedSave (store.ts:607) → reloadTabsFromDisk([path], {discardLocalEdits:true}) → openNoteModel(t.id, t.path, diskContent) at store.ts:1152 → noteModel.ts:191-192 reset version=0, savedVersion=0. The retry write then lands and saveUnchained calls M.markSaved(id, 12, r.path) (noteSession.ts:258); r.path === m.path (same-path re-seed), so the guard passes and noteModel.ts:513 sets savedVersion=12 while version=0. From this moment isDirty() (noteModel.ts:519) returns 12 > 0 → false for the next TWELVE edits. The user types twelve characters, then clicks a wikilink: openNoteTab's departure flush is gated on isNoteDirty(currentTab.id) (store.ts:3239) → false → NO flush → openNoteModel(currentTab.id, filePath, content) at store.ts:3290 replaces the model. Twelve keystrokes are gone from the model, never written to disk, no net (handleFlush's PJ-181 snapshot flag is `SINGLE_OWNERSHIP && !isModelDirty(tab.id)` at NoteEditor.svelte:391 → flagged as an ALREADY-DURABLE snapshot, so resolveNoteContent's staleSnapshot branch at store.ts:2978-3001 rejects and CLEARS it on reopen), no save-health entry, no journal marker. flushAllForAppClose (store.ts:3395) and flushDisposeClearTabs likewise skip the tab. Same shape for any late-resolving save across a reloadTabsFromDisk re-seed (cascade reload, task toggle, structural resolve, merge resolve). Root cause: the model has no generation/epoch — markSaved cannot tell that the object under (id, path) is a NEW model, and openModel resetting version to 0 makes the monotonic savedVersion an absorbing state.
reason: Verified in source: noteModel.openModel (noteModel.ts:169-198) mints a NEW model with version=0/savedVersion=0, and markSaved (noteModel.ts:509-514) is guarded ONLY by path equality and only ever raises savedVersion. There is no generation/epoch in noteModel.ts or noteSession.ts (grepped). So a save that composed version N before a SAME-PATH re-seed passes the guard (r.path === m.path in saveUnchained, noteSession.ts:258) and stamps savedVersion=N onto a version=0 model, making isDirty() (noteModel.ts:517-519) report clean for the next N edits. The guard's own comment claims to prevent this exact class; it demonstrably covers only the different-path case. The harm is real and silent: the departure flush in openNoteTab is gated on isNoteDirty (store.ts:3239), flushAllForAppClose likewise (store.ts:3395), and the outgoing pane's handleFlush bails on filePath !== tab.path (NoteEditor.svelte:338) once the tab is repathed — so edits still inside NotePane's 1500ms debounce are discarded with no banner, no write-ahead net, no journal marker. HOWEVER two candidate claims are refuted and force a downgrade from APP-KILLER: (1) the generalization to "any reloadTabsFromDisk re-seed (cascade reload, task toggle, structural resolve, merge resolve)" is FALSE — PJ-174 #1 (store.ts:1128-1141) deletes any dirty path before openNoteModel (store.ts:1152), and an in-flight save implies a dirty model, so only discardFailedSave (store.ts:607-627, the sole discardLocalEdits:true caller) can re-seed under an in-flight save; openNoteTab/loadTabHistoryEntry AWAIT flushOutgoing, whose save chains behind the in-flight one (saveChains, noteSession.ts:200-239), so no unresolved save survives their re-seed. (2) "Twelve keystrokes never written to disk" is overstated — NotePane's autosave is driven by its own view-level dirty flag (NotePane.svelte:361/586/595), not the model, so handleSave -> saveNoteSession -> compose still writes current model content to disk 1500ms after typing pauses; the exposure is only edits departed-from inside that debounce, i.e. APP-KILLER #2 protection re-opened for up to N edits. Net: a real, silent, unguarded false-clean defect reachable via a compound race (failed save + a retry that SUCCEEDS + the two-click Discard landing inside that write's in-flight window + a fast subsequent nav/close). Fix shape: give NoteModel a monotonic epoch minted in openModel and carried through compose -> markSaved/noteDiskSynced, so a save that resolves after ANY re-seed (same path included) is a no-op.

The user presses Alt+← to navigate tab T back to N, then immediately Ctrl+W. loadTabHistoryEntry (store.ts:1935) awaits resolveNoteContent(filePath, {preserveNet:false}) at :1966, which CONSUMES and clears N's net (store.ts:3011) and returns recoveredFromNet:true. During that await closeTab(T) runs: it flushes (store.ts:3667), calls closeNoteModel(T) at :3682 and openTabs.set(newTabs) at :3714. closeTab does not touch _navTokens, so the supersede check at :1978 passes; flushOutgoing(T) at :1984 finds no tab and returns {ok:true}; the openTabs.update at :2000 matches nothing and no-ops. The net was cleared, disk still holds the pre-failure version, and nothing is on screen. reason: Verified in source, not inferred. loadTabHistoryEntry (store.ts:1935) awaits resolveNoteContent at :1966 with preserveNet: displayOnlyWindow — false in the main window — and store.ts:3011 (`if (!opts.preserveNet) clearWriteAhead(filePath)`) CONSUMES the incoming note's write-ahead entry before returning recoveredFromNet:true. From that point the only restash sites are the three abort paths (:1978, :1985, :1986); there is NO tab-existence check before the swap. Then :2014 openNoteModel → noteSession.open (noteSession.ts:55) → noteModel.openModel (noteModel.ts:169-197) does `models.set(id, m)` UNCONDITIONALLY (no tab check anywhere in the model layer), and :2017 markModelRecoveredFromNet marks it dirty with the recovered bytes. summary: restoreSessionTabs seeds a write-ahead-RECOVERED tab's model born CLEAN (only setting the true disk baseline), so a genuine external edit to that note is adopted with no conflict — and adoptExternalChangeIntoTabs then clears the write-ahead net, destroying the only copy of the user's unsaved failed-save work.
silent_failure_scenario: The user edits note N; the save fails because a sync agent (OneDrive/Syncthing) holds the file; the write-ahead net keeps the edit and the save-health banner shows. The user closes Constellation. On next boot restoreSessionTabs resolves N with {preserveNet:true} (store.ts:3582), gets recoveredFromNet with resolved.diskContent = the true (older) disk bytes, appends the tab and at :3628 calls openNoteModel(t.id, t.path, t.content) — version=0, savedVersion=0, i.e. CLEAN — then at :3635 setModelDiskBaseline(t.id, trueDisk). markRecoveredFromNet is deliberately NOT called here (Gate #8: restore performs zero write-class IPCs), so the model is clean while its content differs from disk. The same sync agent that caused the lock now finishes pulling the newer copy from another device; the watcher fires and adoptExternalChangeIntoTabs runs. At store.ts:1332 externalChangeNoteModel → adoptDisk: isDirty is FALSE (clean by construction), composeModel !== disk, and disk !== diskBaseline (the true baseline, which is exactly what makes a GENUINE change pass) → it ADOPTS. The dirty-conflict branch at :1337 is never reached because the model is clean, so no .conflict sidecar and no banner is raised. Then :1357 `for (const p of adopted) clearWriteAhead(p)` deletes the net. The user's unsaved paragraph is now gone from the screen (replaced by the adopted disk), gone from the net, and was never on disk — with no error anywhere. The PJ-102b restore-half comment (noteModel.ts:462-474) only claims protection against PHANTOM events; the genuine-change case has no protection because born-clean disables the one guard (isDirty) that would have routed it to the sidecar.
reason: Confirmed by reading the code end to end. restoreSessionTabs (store.ts:3582/3628/3635) seeds a write-ahead-recovered tab's model CLEAN (openNoteModel → version 0 = savedVersion 0) and only truth-sets diskBaseline via setModelDiskBaseline; markRecoveredFromNet (noteModel.ts:450-460, the call that dirties the model) is deliberately not invoked on the restore half (noteModel.ts:462-474, Gate #8). adoptDisk (noteModel.ts:534-559) has exactly three gates — isDirty (false by construction), echo composeModel===disk (false, content differs), phantom disk===diskBaseline (false for a GENUINE external change) — so a genuine external write ADOPTS. In adoptExternalChangeIntoTabs the .conflict/banner branch (store.ts:1337) is an `else if (isNoteDirty…)` and is therefore structurally unreachable for this born-clean model, and store.ts:1357 then runs clearWriteAhead(p) for every adopter, which (store.ts:366-373) deletes the entry from both the in-memory map and the `constellation-wab` localStorage blob. The net is provably the ONLY copy at that moment: saveHealth is an in-memory writable (store.ts:414) that does not survive restart, so no banner is showing after boot; a failed save writes no disk sidecar (NoteEditor.svelte:391-414 only re-stashes the net); and tests/mig-100/restore.test.ts:248-250 states the invariant outright ("the model is born clean, so the net is the ONLY durable copy until a real save replaces it"). The clear at :1357 is a non-save event, violating resolveNoteContent's own contract at store.ts:3009 that the net "survives until a real durable save replaces it". Reachability checks all pass: WATCHER_ADOPT_ENABLED = true (store.ts:282); a failed-save net entry has `snapshot` omitted so PJ-181's staleSnapshot rejection (store.ts:2978) does not fire; a previously-saved note is identityProven by cid so the net is accepted (store.ts:2946-2948); requireDisk is satisfied because the file exists. Concrete failure: save of note N fails under a sync-agent file lock → net holds the only copy, banner up → user quits (PJ-103 close-flush retries and fails under the same lock) → reboot → restore shows the recovered text, model born clean, baseline = true (older) disk, no banner → the sync agent finishes pulling the newer copy from another device → watcher fires → clean adopt replaces the on-screen text with disk and clearWriteAhead deletes the net. The user's paragraph is gone from screen, gone from memory, gone from localStorage, never on disk, with no error, banner, or sidecar anywhere. The nearby refutations do not cover this: the store.ts:3505-3511 refutation concerns pendingCidEnsure/cid-less content at a different site, the PJ-102b phantom guard only covers disk===baseline, and preserveNet protects the net from the READ path, not the ADOPT path. The same shape recurs at the cascade site (store.ts:1152/1161: clean tabs force-adopted via openNoteModel, then the net cleared), which corroborates rather than refutes. Suggested fix direction: on the restore half, either mark the recovered model dirty without a write-class IPC (so the arbiter routes a genuine external change to the .conflict sidecar), or make the clearWriteAhead at :1357 (and :1161) skip any path whose current model content still differs from disk — i.e. only a durable save may burn the net.

summary: The rename cascade's rewrite regex only matches `[[Old]]` and `[[Old|…]]`, so it silently skips the app's own canonical predicate-first typed-link form `[[type::Old]]` and every heading/block-anchor link `[[Old#Heading]]` / `[[Old^id]]`; the rename then reports full success with an empty `failed` list.
silent_failure_scenario: User writes a Living Link with the editor's own autocomplete: `src/lib/editor/completions.ts:97` and `:183` insert `[[supports::Alpha]]` (the comment at :178 calls this "canonical predicate-first form"), and `search.rs:6841` parses exactly that shape into note_links. User then renames note "Alpha" → "Alpha v2" with Auto-update links ON. `update_links_on_rename` builds `\[\[(Alpha)(\]\]|\|)` — after `[[` the text is `supports::Alpha`, so the regex cannot match. `rewrite_wikilinks_in_text` returns the content unchanged, `gate_rmw` writes nothing, the file is never added to `result.rewritten` NOR to `result.failed` (that arm is only for write errors, libraries.rs:6587), so `handleRenameComplete`'s new failure toast (+layout.svelte:7355) stays silent and the rename reports success. Every typed link on disk still reads `[[supports::Alpha]]`. It keeps resolving only because `rename_item` stamped an `aliases:` entry — the moment the user later creates or renames any note to the freed title "Alpha", exact-title resolution beats the alias and every one of those typed links silently re-points to a DIFFERENT note (cross-note bleed in the knowledge graph, with the referring .md still saying `supports::Alpha`). Same miss applies to `[[Alpha#Section]]` / `![[Alpha#Section]]`, which `embeds.rs:301` parses as first-class forms. Repro: create A.md containing `[[supports::Alpha]]`, `[[Alpha#Intro]]` and `[[Alpha]]`; rename Alpha → Alpha v2; only the third link is rewritten, with no error anywhere.
reason: Verified in source. The cascade's only rewrite pattern is libraries.rs:6406 `\[\[({old})(\]\]|\|)`, which requires the title to sit immediately after `[[` and be followed by `]]` or `|`. It therefore cannot match the app's OWN canonical predicate-first typed link `[[type::Old]]` — emitted by the editor autocomplete (completions.ts:97 and :183, "canonical predicate-first form"), rendered by livePreview.ts:1477-1497, and parsed as canonical by search.rs:6841 parse_link_body — nor any anchor form `[[Old#Heading]]` / `[[Old^block]]` / `![[Old#Heading]]`, which embeds.rs:295-310 and resolve_wikilink_cross_library_impl (libraries.rs:2865) both treat as first-class. A grep of every regex::escape / replace_all site in src-tauri confirms there is NO second cascade pass and no `::`- or `#`-aware variant; the cascade test block (libraries.rs:6882-6990) covers only the legacy predicate-LAST combos, and the doc comment at :6605 enumerates only those — the regex was never updated when predicate-first became canonical. The failure is fully silent: in update_links_recursive (libraries.rs:6576-6597) an unchanged file takes the `Ok(_) => {}` arm, so it lands in neither `rewritten` nor `failed` (`failed` is populated only from the gate_rmw error arm), and +layout.svelte:7353 derives its cascade toast solely from result.failed + failed_truncated — so the 2026-08-01 failure toast cannot fire and the rename reports plain success. Concrete repro: A.md containing `[[supports::Alpha]]`, `[[Alpha#Intro]]`, `[[Alpha]]`; rename Alpha -> Alpha v2 with auto-update ON; only the third is rewritten, A.md is never in `failed`, no error anywhere. Divergence escalates because find_note_by_name_or_alias (libraries.rs:2971) resolves stem -> title -> alias, so a later note carrying the freed title "Alpha" beats the rename-stamped alias and every stale typed link silently re-points to a different note; in-app reuse is guarded by the alias-aware resolve_title_collision (libraries.rs:2758), but an externally created Alpha.md (Obsidian/Syncthing — supported sync) is not, nor is the user deleting the accumulated alias or choosing Overwrite. Not APP-KILLER: the rename-stamped alias keeps the stale links resolving immediately after the rename and the collision dialog blocks in-app title reuse, so there is no immediate loss or corruption and the .md content stays intact and repairable.

summary: The note_meta_sky_au rename trigger rewrites sky_links.target_name for EVERY edge in the universe that names the renamed note, with no identity qualification — so renaming one note silently re-points thousands of edges that belong to same-named homonyms, and nothing in the codebase ever rebuilds sky_links.
silent_failure_scenario: The live universe contains SEVEN notes whose display name is "Doi (identifier)" (Literature/Classical, Music/Theory & Practice, Linguistics/Core Areas, Philosophy/Ancient Philosophy, Biology/Cell Biology, Computer Science/Algorithms, Physics/Classical Mechanics). ONE of them — Biology\Cell Biology\Doi (identifier).md — was renamed to "Doi (identifier) test". note_meta_sky_au fired `UPDATE sky_links SET target_name = COALESCE(NEW.name_lower, LOWER(NEW.name)) WHERE target_name = COALESCE(OLD.name_lower, LOWER(OLD.name))` (search.rs:5432-5435). The WHERE keys on the NAME only — no source_path, no cid, no restriction to edges that actually resolved to the renamed note — so all 4,359 sky_links rows naming `doi (identifier)` were rewritten to `doi (identifier) test`, including the ~4,300 that belong to the other six notes and whose `[[...]]` wikilinks on disk were never touched. note_links still says `doi (identifier)`. MEASURED NOW in search.db: 4,371 sky_links rows have no matching active note_links row (4,359 of them the `doi (identifier) test` name), and 4,308 active cognitive note_links have no sky_links row at all — across 4,315 distinct source notes. The same shape is present for four other renames ('apple tree fruit drift' ×4, 'المعزة ن2' ×2, 'الزراعة المستدامة ن2', 'a v2', 'anchor2', 'hum2'), so it is systematic, not a one-off. Nothing heals it: index_repair.rs:415 states it in terms — "nothing in the codebase rebuilds sky_links — recompute_all_sky only UPDATEs sky_nodes columns" — and sky_backfill's INSERT OR IGNORE is one-shot behind the 'sky' schema stamp. Net user-visible effect with zero error surfaced: Sky View draws ~4,300 edges into a node that only one note carries, and omits ~4,300 real edges of the graph; every sky-derived read is wrong and stays wrong forever.
reason:
CONFIRMED as a real, silent, permanent index-divergence defect — but on a corrected mechanism and at a lower severity than filed.

CODE (read, not inferred): search.rs:5428-5435 `note_meta_sky_au` executes `UPDATE sky_links SET target_name = COALESCE(NEW.name_lower, LOWER(NEW.name)) WHERE target_name = COALESCE(OLD.name_lower, LOWER(OLD.name)) AND OLD<>NEW`. The WHERE qualifies on NAME ONLY — no source_path, no cid_cn, no restriction to edges that actually resolved to the renamed note.

REACHABILITY (everyday, and the in-file comment is stale): index_note_impl writes note_meta via `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT(path) DO UPDATE` (search.rs ~7666), which fires AFTER UPDATE — so the trigger's own comment at search.rs:5441-5444 ("index_note uses DELETE+INSERT, which fires AD+AI not AU ... defensive coverage for test code") is FALSE today. note_meta.name = frontmatter `title:` else file stem (search.rs ~7429), so simply editing a note's title property fires the trigger with the path unchanged. That is exactly the live shape: the file is still `Biology\Cell Biology\Doi (identifier).md` while note_meta.name = 'Doi (identifier) test'.

MEASURED IN THE LIVE DB (E:\Constellation Universes\Eisa Cognitive Knowledge\.constellation\search.db, read-only): 7 notes named 'Doi (identifier)', one renamed. sky_links holds 4,359 rows 'doi (identifier) test' + 52 'doi (identifier)'; note_links holds 4,360 active rows, ALL still 'doi (identifier)'. Exact anti-joins: 4,359 sky_links rows have NO matching active note_links row; 4,308 real active note_links edges have NO sky_links row at all; 52 source notes already carry BOTH the phantom and a re-added real edge.

NOTHING HEALS IT (verified): the only three `DELETE FROM sky_links` sites are the two note_links triggers keyed on exact (source_path, target_name, link_type) — a phantom's target_name matches no note_links row, so it can never be deleted — and note_meta_sky_ad keyed on source_path. sky_backfill.rs:286 is INSERT OR IGNORE, one-shot behind the 'sky' schema stamp, and never deletes. index_repair.rs:415 states it in the codebase's own words: "nothing in the codebase rebuilds sky_links — recompute_all_sky only UPDATEs sky_nodes columns." Because index_note diffs edges, unchanged edges are never rewritten, so the phantom persists and each later edit of a source note ADDS a correct duplicate beside it — monotonically accumulating double-counted edges. No error is surfaced anywhere; it is a pure SQL trigger side effect.

USER-VISIBLE, SILENT: cache.rs:1163 resolves sky_links.target_name straight to a node id and bumps link_count; that feeds skyLinks in +layout.svelte:1166 → Sky View, GraphMindView, and Sight v3 community detection. Those surfaces draw ~4,300 edges into a node no wikilink names and omit ~4,300 real edges of the graph.

WHERE I DEPART FROM THE CANDIDATE: the framing "renaming one note re-points thousands of edges" is not inherently the bug. With no homonym the blanket rewrite is CORRECT and necessary — sky_nodes.id becomes the new folded name, so edges must follow or they fall to cache.rs's tier-3 unresolved branch and lose link_count. The defect is strictly the missing identity qualification under homonyms. Note also that cache.rs:1147-1152 documents note_aliases as the DESIGNED rename handler ("the alias table maps that old name back to the renamed note's current path"), so the trigger is a second, conflicting mechanism.

summary: `unquote` strips a value's surrounding quotes WITHOUT decoding YAML escape sequences, so the projection carries the escape SYNTAX as data; the moment the user touches that key, `serializeLine` re-serializes the escaped text and the note's real value is permanently replaced by its source form.
silent_failure_scenario: REPRODUCED by running the real parser + composer. Note has `aliases:` with an item `- 'O''Brien'` (correct YAML for the alias O'Brien — produced by Obsidian, by an import, or by hand). `parseFrontmatter` (store.ts:2536 → unquote at 2315) projects the item as the literal string `O''Brien`, not `O'Brien`. The user adds ONE unrelated alias in the Properties panel. `touchedSince` marks `aliases` touched, `plan` emits a `set`, and `composeFrontmatter` splices the seq and re-emits it from the projection: the .md now reads `- O''Brien` (a plain scalar), which re-parses as the string `O''Brien`. The alias the user actually had is gone from the file and from `note_aliases`, so `[[O'Brien]]` stops resolving. Identical mechanism for double-quoted values: `title: "The \"Real\" Thing"` projects as `The \"Real\" Thing` and, on any edit of that key, is written back as the UNQUOTED plain scalar `title: The \"Real\" Thing!`, i.e. two literal backslashes injected into the note's title — which is what `extract_frontmatter_title` and the rename/wikilink cascade key on. No error, no banner, and the rewritten YAML re-parses cleanly so nothing downstream notices. The same undecoded `unquote` feeds the flow-seq splitter (2352), the ikhtilāf field reader (2507) and the scalar path (2576).
reason: Reproduced with the real modules (vitest, temp file removed). noteModel.openModel (noteModel.ts:184) builds both `props` and `base.props` from store.parseFrontmatter, whose only quote handling is `unquote` (store.ts:2315) — strips a matching pair, never decodes escapes; yamlDoc.projectProps (the library-accurate decoder) has NO callers, so it is dark. composeModel (USE_YAML_DOC=true) diffs that escaped projection into composeFrontmatter, so any key the user EDITS is re-serialized from the escape SYNTAX. Confirmed cases: (1) `aliases: - 'O''Brien'` (real value O'Brien) projects as `O''Brien`; adding one unrelated alias writes `- O''Brien` as a plain scalar, which re-parses as O''Brien — the real alias is gone from the .md. (2) Self-inflicted and COMPOUNDING: serializeLine itself emits `"Ibn Khaldun's \"Muqaddimah\": a reading"` for ordinary typed text (apostrophe + double quote + colon-space); three successive edits of that key produced on disk `\\\"` → `\\\\\\\"` → `\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"` — backslashes DOUBLE per edit, i.e. the very 'accumulate backslashes on quoted values' defect the yamlDoc header claims G4 fixed, unfixed because the diff base is not the library's projection. Same compounding on list items while the user merely appends aliases. Refutations tested and failed: untouched keys ARE byte-perfect (verified) but the scenario is an edited key where samePropRow sees a diff; frontmatterIsRewritable passes (the YAML is well-formed) so the PJ-207 §15 refusal banner never fires; no error, no banner, and the rewritten YAML re-parses cleanly so nothing downstream notices; it does not self-correct, it compounds; and the corrupted title is what extract_frontmatter_title (libraries.rs:2016) and the rename/alias/wikilink resolution key on. Fix direction: route parseFrontmatter's scalar/list/ikhtilaf value paths through the yaml library (projectProps) instead of `unquote`, so the diff base and the serializer speak the same values.

summary: `if (saving) return;` silently discards a debounced save that fires while a previous write is in flight — but NotePane already cleared its `dirty` flag before the call, so nothing re-arms the save, while the in-flight save's compare-and-clear wipes the write-ahead net that was the newer keystrokes' only crash copy.
silent_failure_scenario: Note lives on a synced/AV-scanned folder so a `write_note` takes ~2.5s. t=0: NotePane's 1500ms debounce fires → doSave() sets `dirty = false` (NotePane.svelte:361-362) BEFORE calling onsave → handleSave sets `saving = true` (NoteEditor.svelte:287) and starts saveNoteSession, which calls setNet(path, contentV1) then awaits the write. t=0.3s: user types a paragraph → model advances to V2 via onDocChange→editBody (NoteEditor.svelte:770), `dirty = true`, debounce re-armed. t=1.8s: debounce fires → doSave() sets `dirty = false` again → handleSave hits `if (saving) return` at line 284 and DROPS the save. Nothing reschedules it: the debounce timer is null, and the 30s idle timer (NotePane.svelte:1015) calls doSave() which returns immediately on `!dirty` (line 361). t=2.5s: the V1 write completes; markSaved is version-gated so the model correctly stays dirty, but `clearNetIf(r.path, contentV1)` (noteSession.ts:260 → store.ts:382) finds the net still holding exactly contentV1 and CLEARS it. The user now stops typing. State: the paragraph exists ONLY in the in-memory model — not on disk, not in writeAheadBuffer, not in localStorage `constellation-wab`, with no pending write and no banner. A hard crash / power loss / OS kill at this point loses it silently (beforeunload's doFlush→setWriteAhead re-stash only covers a graceful unload). The `saving` guard is also now redundant: noteSession.save already serializes per-id via `saveChains` (noteSession.ts:200-239), so the drop buys nothing.
reason: Verified end-to-end in source. NotePane.doSave() clears view-level `dirty` BEFORE invoking onsave (NotePane.svelte:361-362), and NoteEditor.handleSave's `if (saving) return` (NoteEditor.svelte:284) sits ahead of editBody/markRecentWrite/saveNoteSession, so a dropped call stashes nothing. Nothing re-arms: the debounce timer nulled itself (NotePane.svelte:595), the 30s idle timer (NotePane.svelte:1015) and the visibilitychange handler (NotePane.svelte:374) both short-circuit on `!dirty`, and grep of +layout.svelte shows the only periodic sweep is the save-health retry (line 1745-1751), gated on $saveHealth.size — which is empty because no write failed. Meanwhile the in-flight V1 write completes successfully: markSaved is version-gated (noteModel.ts:509-513) so the model correctly stays dirty, but clearWriteAheadIf (store.ts:382-386) clears the net because its compare-and-clear only protects when a NEWER net exists — and the drop is exactly what prevented a newer setNet. Result: the newest keystrokes live only in the in-memory model, with no pending write, no write-ahead buffer, no localStorage `constellation-wab` entry, no save-health banner, and no unsaved indicator anywhere in the tab UI (isDirty has no UI consumer; only NoteEditor.svelte:391 reads it, inside the flush path). Reachability is real: `saving` stays true for the full write_note round-trip, which under gate_write (write_gate.rs:394-457 — per-path mutex, path validation, full read_to_string for self-attestation, atomic_write with fsync, then journal_ext) exceeds 1500ms on an AV-scanned/synced folder or when the IPC pool is busy with a multi-second derived-data command; it also spans a chained predecessor save (noteSession.ts:211-224). The candidate's secondary claim is also correct — save() already serializes per id via saveChains (noteSession.ts:200-239), so the guard buys no ordering safety and dropping it (or re-setting `dirty` on the drop) is the safe fix. Not raised above MED because it destroys the crash net rather than deleting data directly: the model retains the content and every graceful path recovers it — one further keystroke re-arms the debounce, and tab switch (flushIfDirty), tab close, app close (flushAllForAppClose) and beforeunload→doFlush→handleFlush's setWriteAhead(..., snapshot=!isModelDirty) all re-stash. summary: handleSave's `if (saving) return;` re-entrancy guard DISCARDS a debounced save request whose `dirty` flag NotePane already cleared at NotePane.svelte:362 — and nothing ever retries it, so the note's newest content can sit only in the in-memory model indefinitely with no error, no banner, and no write-ahead net refresh.
silent_failure_scenario: NotePane.doSave() (NotePane.svelte:360-367) clears `dirty = false` on line 362 BEFORE calling `onsave?.()`, and every early-return in NoteEditor.handleSave sits after that point. Recipe: user types in a large note; the 1500 ms debounce fires at T and handleSave sets `saving = true` and awaits `saveNoteSession` → `writeNote` → the Rust write gate. The user keeps typing (each keystroke pushes the rope to the model via onDocChange, and re-arms the debounce), then STOPS. At T+1500 the debounce fires: doSave sets `dirty = false`, snapshots the text, calls onsave → handleSave hits `if (saving) return;` at line 284 and drops it on the floor. Now: (a) NotePane's `dirty` is false, so the 30 s idle timer (NotePane.svelte:1015, `if (!dirty) return`) and the visibilitychange save (NotePane.svelte:374) are both dead; (b) no keystroke follows, so the debounce is never re-armed; (c) `save()` was never entered, so `setNet` never ran and the write-ahead net still holds the OLDER composition from T; (d) no saveHealth entry exists, so the ~10 s auto-retry loop (+layout.svelte:1745-1751) and retrySaveFailure (store.ts:512) never touch it. The last seconds of typing now exist ONLY in the non-reactive model Map: a hard kill / power loss / webview crash loses them outright, and until the user navigates away, closes the tab, or closes the app (the flushOutgoing/flushAllForAppClose departure paths) the note on disk, in FTS5, in the second screen and in every derived surface is silently behind what is on screen. The guard is also redundant by construction: noteSession.save already serializes concurrent saves per id via `saveChains` (noteSession.ts:200-239, the PJ-103 adversarial-review fix) precisely so a newer composition writes last — so chaining is the designed behaviour and this drop defeats it. Severe tail: `saving` is only reset by `.finally()` on the returned promise (NoteEditor.svelte:321); in the CHAINED branch `save()` calls `M.compose` synchronously at noteSession.ts:219, so a synchronous throw there escapes before `.finally` is attached and leaves `saving` stuck true — after which EVERY save from that NoteEditor instance is silently dropped for the life of the tab. REFUTED sub-claims: (1) the "saving stuck true for the life of the tab" tail — M.compose returns a result object and cannot throw (noteModel.ts:487-498) and setWriteAhead swallows its own exception with an empty catch (store.ts:348-352), so no synchronous throw escapes save() before .finally attaches; (2) HIGH severity — write_note is #[tauri::command(async)] (libraries.rs:780) so it does not queue behind main-thread work, a >1500 ms round trip needs a genuinely slow/contended write (AV scan, cloud-synced universe path, or chaining behind another save site), and permanent loss additionally requires an abnormal termination (crash/kill/power loss) before the next keystroke or any departure flush, since normal quit (flushAllForAppClose), navigation (flushIfDirty), tab close and universe switch (flushAllDirtyTabs, store.ts:3368) all still persist the model. That pane's onMount overwrites `lastView`/`lastPath` with the read-only view for path P. The user now invokes the emoji/icon picker: `getActiveEditor()` returns the preview's view, and `view.dispatch({changes})` APPLIES — CodeMirror's `EditorState.readOnly` facet is advisory and blocks input handlers/commands, not programmatic transactions. The insert is discarded with no error and no trace, while the user saw it land. The same aliasing makes `getActiveEditorForPath(P)` hand a read-only view to the template paths, which then either write into a doomed doc or take their 'no live editor' refusal branch for a note that IS in fact open and editable.

summary: The post-save re-embed is a bare `invoke(...).catch(() => {})` at both editor save sites, so a failed embedding write leaves `note_embeddings` permanently stale for that note with zero surface — three lines below a `reindexNote` call that was deliberately given bounded retry plus a surfaced `indexHealthError`.
silent_failure_scenario: In `handleSave`'s onSaved (NoteEditor.svelte:306-311) and `handleFlush`'s onSaved (:406-411), `invoke('constellation_embed_notes', {notes:[{path, name, content: text}], force: true}).catch(() => {})` swallows every failure. Recipe: semantic search is enabled; the user rewrites a note's body; the durable disk write succeeds so `markSaved`/`noteDiskSynced` run and the model goes CLEAN; the embed IPC then fails (embeddings model not loaded yet at that moment, a transient rusqlite writer-lock contention on the `INSERT OR REPLACE INTO note_embeddings` at src-tauri/src/embeddings.rs:469, or an OOM/dimension error). Nothing retries: the model is clean so no further save fires for that content, `retrySaveFailure` (store.ts:512) is gated on a saveHealth entry that was never created, and the only other writer is the explicit bulk `embedNotes` action (store.ts:4233). The asymmetry is the tell: the sibling `void reindexNote(...)` on the immediately preceding line was given a two-attempt retry and a user-visible `indexHealthError` (store.ts:3924-3948) exactly because a silent index failure was ruled unacceptable; the embed on the next line got neither. Identical bare catches sit at store.ts:648-651 (navFlushEnv) and store.ts:1824-1827 (saveTabContent), so every save path in the app shares the hole.
reason: Grounded in the real code at all four sites. NoteEditor.svelte:306-311 (handleSave onSaved) and :407-412 (handleFlush onSaved) are literally `invoke('constellation_embed_notes', {notes:[…], force:true}).catch(() => {})`, mirrored at store.ts:648-651 (navFlushEnv) and store.ts:1824-1827 (prop-save runPostSave). The Rust command does reject on reachable, in-repo-documented conditions: `ensure_engine` failure, `search_state.db.lock()` failure / "Search database not initialized", and the `INSERT OR REPLACE INTO note_embeddings` at embeddings.rs:468-471 mapped to "DB write failed" — a SQLITE_BUSY past the 5s busy_timeout is exactly the transient that store.ts:3922 cites as the reason reindexNote was GIVEN a retry ("a backfill can hold it longer than the 5s busy_timeout"). No self-correction exists: the boot backfill (+layout.svelte:6228-6269) only fires when embedded_count < allNotes.length AND calls embedNotes without `force`, so embeddings.rs:446-457 skips any path that already has a row — a stale-but-present row is invisible to that gate twice over; index_repair.rs contains ZERO references to embeddings, so PJ-207's drift notice / Repair now / Full re-read do not cover this table at all; reconcile.rs only migrates note_embeddings.path, never content; constellation_search_reindex does not re-embed. note_embeddings is named a source-of-truth index by the inspection charter itself (.claude/workflows/safety-inspection.js:49). One correction to the candidate's wording: "permanently / indefinitely" is overstated — the next SUCCESSFUL save of that same note re-fires with force:true and heals it; the real exposure is a note edited once inside the bad window and then left untouched. summary: The cascade walks ONLY the renamed note's own library root (`lib.path` from the longest-prefix `libraryForPath`), so when the renamed note lives in a nested registered library, every referrer elsewhere in the Universe keeps `[[OldTitle]]` — silently, with the rename reporting success.
silent_failure_scenario: MIG-108 puts every library UNDER the Universe root, and `libraryForPath` (+layout.svelte:6821-6831) returns the LONGEST prefix, so a note at `<root>/Research/Alpha.md` (where `Research` is a registered library) resolves to lib.path = `<root>/Research`. `updateLinksOnRename(lib.path, …)` → `update_links_recursive(Path::new("<root>/Research"))` walks only that subtree. But wikilinks resolve UNIVERSE-wide (`resolve_wikilink_cross_library`, libraries.rs:2740; the "It is ONE universe" ruling), so a note in the root `universe_notes` library or a sibling library that contains `[[Alpha]]` is a live, resolvable referrer that the walk never visits. It is therefore absent from both `result.rewritten` and `result.failed`, the cascade-failure toast at :7355 never fires, and the tab reload at :7392 never touches it. On disk, those notes permanently point at a title that no longer exists (kept alive only by the `aliases:` stamp, with the same later-collision hazard as the typed-link finding). Asymmetric and therefore easy to miss in testing: renaming a note that lives in the ROOT library walks the whole Universe and looks correct, so the bug only appears once the user creates a second library.
reason: Real and reachable, but less severe than filed. VERIFIED: +layout.svelte:7285 `libraryForPath(oldPath)` is a longest-prefix resolver (:6821-6832) over $libraryStats, which `get_all_library_stats`→`load_all_libraries` (libraries.rs:1039) populates with the root `universe_notes` entry AND every nested library. :7342 passes only `lib.path` into `update_links_on_rename` (libraries.rs:6386), whose `update_links_recursive` (:6527) is a plain read_dir recursion bounded by that single root. There is exactly one cascade call site in the codebase and no second leg. Link resolution, by contrast, is universe-wide: `resolve_wikilink_cross_library_impl` (:2926-2941) explicitly loops "Search other libraries", and the editor's own wikilink autocomplete is fed by `allNotes` (+layout.svelte:4254 = core.notes across libraries), so cross-library [[Title]] referrers are app-created and first-class. RECIPE: two libraries under one root (the MIG-108 norm) — `<root>/Research` (registered) and the root `universe_notes` library. Note `<root>/Research/Alpha.md`, referrer `<root>/Notes/Beta.md` containing `[[Alpha]]` (offered by the app's own autocomplete). Rename Alpha → Alpha v2. lib.path resolves to `<root>/Research`; the walk never visits Beta.md. Beta is absent from BOTH `result.rewritten` and `result.failed`, so the cascade-failure toast at :7355 structurally cannot fire, and the setting's own promise is "Update all links when a note is renamed" (en.json:251). Asymmetric and easy to miss: renaming a note in the ROOT library resolves lib.path == <root> and walks the whole Universe, so single-library testing looks correct. This is the same shape as the already-fixed 2026-07-24 finding quoted in the comment at :7276-7282 — that fix corrected WHICH library is walked, not that ONE library is walked while the link namespace is the Universe. PARTIAL REFUTATIONS (why MED, not HIGH): the rename stamps the old title into the renamed note's own FRONTMATTER `aliases:` (libraries.rs:1280, update_frontmatter_title :2043-2190) — durable on disk, not merely the DB 'rename' row (:1649, which index_note preserves since search.rs:7867 deletes only source='frontmatter' rows). So the stale [[OldTitle]] still RESOLVES; the link is not broken. Backlinks are alias-aware (incoming_links_backfill rehearsal pins "dedupe-by-source, alias resolution"), so no backlinks are lost and no index/disk divergence is created (the un-walked referrer's note_links.target_name still matches its own untouched file). A later note claiming the old title is warned by the universe-wide, alias-aware `resolve_title_collision` (:2765-2780). NET: no data loss and no broken links today, but a documented "all links" operation is silently incomplete in the documented normal multi-library configuration, reports success, and leaves referrers permanently rendering a title that no longer exists — kept alive only by an alias line the user can delete, with the resolution-ambiguity hazard that follows. Fix direction: walk every library returned by resolve_universe_libraries (or the Universe root) rather than the single owning library, keeping the freeze/flush/markCascading protections scoped per library.

summary: The PJ-207 §15 back-resolution of note_links.target_cid_cn lives only in note_meta_sky_ai (AFTER INSERT), but index_note writes note_meta by UPSERT — so a cid that arrives after a note's first index (the documented lazy first-open injection) never resolves the edges waiting on it, and no reconcile exists.

That premise is false: search.rs:7551-7559 documents that MIG-024 §0 replaced DELETE+INSERT with `INSERT … ON CONFLICT(path) DO UPDATE` (the statement at search.rs:7666-7686), there is no `DELETE FROM note_meta` anywhere in index_note, and note_meta_sky_au (search.rs:5411) has no target_cid_cn statement and a WHEN gated on path/name/library_name only. The user later OPENS B in the main window; store.ts:3147 invokes ensure_cid_cn_cmd, which writes the identity into B's frontmatter, and store.ts:3170 fires reindexNote(B) → reindex_single_note → index_note → the UPSERT takes the UPDATE arm because B's row already exists → note_meta_sky_ai never fires → every inbound edge to B keeps a blank target_cid_cn permanently, healing only if each individual source note A_i happens to be re-saved. Nothing reconciles the column (grep: target_cid_cn appears in no reconcile/converge/index_repair path; mig003_step2_backfill at search.rs:4209-4215 keys on target_path, which is unset for name-resolved links). MEASURED live: 1,018 note_links rows carry a blank target_cid_cn, and 576 of those resolve by name to a note_meta row that DOES have a cid. Consumer impact, silent: review.rs:148-155 requires `jl.target_cid_cn IS NOT NULL AND jl.target_cid_cn != ''` to join a dependency, so those 576 load-bearing dependencies are invisible to the Reviewer's Mode-2 staleness lens — editing such a dependency never marks its dependents stale, and the Reviewer shows nothing wrong.
reason: Mechanism verified in source and corroborated by the live index. The PJ-207 §15 back-resolution of note_links.target_cid_cn exists ONLY inside note_meta_sky_ai (AFTER INSERT ON note_meta, search.rs:5345-5374), and its own comment justifies that placement with a premise that is factually false: it claims "index_note re-indexes by DELETE+INSERT". index_note actually writes note_meta by UPSERT (`INSERT … ON CONFLICT(path) DO UPDATE`, search.rs:7666-7686, documented as the deliberate MIG-024 §0 replacement of DELETE+INSERT at 7551-7559), and there is no `DELETE FROM note_meta` anywhere in index_note (grep: the only occurrences are reconcile-removal at 3444, delete_note at 11963, and the libraries.rs rename path). The UPDATE arm therefore fires note_meta_sky_au (5405), whose WHEN is gated on path/name/library_name only and whose body contains no target_cid_cn statement; note_meta_au (4865) is FTS-only; the stratum/maturity AU triggers write sky_nodes only. No other trigger or code path writes target_cid_cn except index_note's own OUTGOING-edge resolver (7917-7924), which never touches edges pointing INTO the reindexed note, and mig003_step2_backfill (4209-4215), which keys on target_path. resolve_incoming_target_paths (2342) only returns paths for aggregate recompute and writes no cid. Reachable path: an externally-created note B is first indexed with cid_cn='' (7450); sources A1..An already containing [[B]] get target_cid_cn NULL; the user later opens B in the main window, store.ts:3147 invokes ensure_cid_cn_cmd which injects the identity, store.ts:3170 fires reindexNote(B) → the UPSERT takes the UPDATE arm → the AI trigger never fires → every inbound edge keeps a blank identity permanently. Measured on the Boss's live universe (copy of search.db, 234,899 edges): 1,018 note_links rows carry a blank target_cid_cn, ALL status='active'; 0 of them have target_path set, so mig003_step2_backfill can never reach any of them; 576 resolve by name_lower to a note_meta row holding a real cid; 207 of those are load-bearing link types; and 245 of the resolvable-blank rows have a source note present in review_schedule. Silent consumer impact confirmed: review.rs:145-158 (stale_probe_sql) joins `note_meta dep ON dep.cid_cn = jl.target_cid_cn` and requires target_cid_cn IS NOT NULL AND != '', so those load-bearing dependencies are invisible to the Reviewer's Mode-2 staleness lens — editing such a dependency never marks its dependents stale and the Reviewer surfaces no error or warning. Every refutation avenue failed: no reconcile/converge/index_repair path touches the column, the PJ-207 drift notice counts notes rather than edges, and the AU trigger's WHEN cannot fire on a cid-only change. Severity is MED, not higher, because the .md files are untouched (the wikilink text is intact, so this is derived-index divergence rather than source-of-truth loss) and it is repairable — any save of the source note re-resolves its edges, and the PJ-207 §14 Full re-read door (search.rs:11700-11717) re-indexes every note with force and would heal all of them. Both remedies are user-initiated with no signal that they are needed. Honest limit: the DB alone cannot distinguish how many of the existing 1,018 arose via the post-index cid injection versus a pre-trigger backlog, but the code proves the path remains open going forward.

(prop.value ? prop.value.split(',')… )`, so a `sources` value that reached disk as a SCALAR still draws pills. `sources`/`content_type` are not in `LIST_KEYS` (store.ts:153-162), so `detectPropertyType` types them `text` and `parseFrontmatter` leaves `listItems` undefined. [])` — an empty array — and calls `applyTaxonomySelection(idx, new Set([]))`, which sets `type:'list'`, `listItems: []`, `value: ''`. The debounced commit emits `set sources = []` and compose writes `sources: []`. reason: Verified in source. []` with no fallback. summary: `link_library_as_universe` unconditionally overwrites `settings.json`, `workspaces.json`, `property-types.json`, `collections.json` (all with `.ok()`) and `libraries.json` with empty defaults whenever `.constellation/universe.json` is absent — even when `.constellation/` is fully populated with the user's data. Its sibling `migrate_legacy_data` guards each of the same writes with `if !exists()` (universe.rs:1941-1952).
silent_failure_scenario: A user syncs their Universe with Syncthing/OneDrive/iCloud (CLAUDE.md: 'Sync is the user's choice'). A conflict resolution renames `universe.json` to `universe.sync-conflict-….json`, or the user deletes it to 'reset' the universe, or a restore-from-backup lands `.constellation/` without it. The Universe now fails `open_existing_universe` (universe.rs:1226: 'not a valid Constellation universe'), so the user takes the other door the setup screen offers — 'Link an existing Markdown folder' (UniverseSetup.svelte:130 → `link_library_as_universe`). The gate at universe.rs:1329 tests only `cdir.join("universe.json").exists()`, sees false, and falls through to the create path: line 1371 writes a ONE-ENTRY `libraries.json` over a registry that held every library in the Universe, then lines 1375-1379 write `"[]"`/`"{}"` over `collections.json` (every Collection and every Starred note), `settings.json`, `workspaces.json` and `property-types.json` — each with `.ok()`, so even an I/O failure is discarded. The command returns Ok, the UI advances to step 2 and reports success. Every collection, saved workspace, property-type assignment and library registration is gone with no error at any layer.
reason:
The unguarded-write defect is real and verified, but the candidate's stated trigger is not — I am confirming a narrower, grounded failure.

VERIFIED CODE FACTS: universe.rs:1329 gates only on `cdir.join("universe.json").exists()`. On false it falls through to 1370-1379, which writes a one-entry `libraries.json` (`?`) and `"[]"`/`"{}"` over `bookmarks/settings/workspaces/property-types/collections.json` with `.ok()` — no existence check, no error propagation. The sibling `migrate_legacy_data` (1941-1952) guards each identical write with `if !exists()`, and `link_library_as_universe` — unlike `open_existing_universe` (1216) — never calls `migrate_to_constellation`. Reachable from UniverseSetup.svelte:416 -> handleLinkLibrary (124-139), the third door on the setup screen ("Bring In a Library / Copy or move an existing folder of notes into this Universe", en.json:2324), which +layout.svelte:3457/3485 shows whenever the registry resolves empty or no universe activates. On success the command returns Ok and the wizard advances to step 2. No error at any layer.

WHAT I COULD NOT GROUND (so I do not assert it): a `.constellation/` populated with settings/collections/workspaces but missing `universe.json`. I searched for a producer and found none — `set_aside_corrupt` (universe.rs:294) is applied only to the app-data registry (line 129), never to universe.json; `migrate_to_constellation` moves universe.json FIRST (line 380); mig108 `take_snapshot` only copies (521-528); the `.constellation/` dirs created by canonical.rs:690 and importers.rs:950 hold only a `canonical` marker / classifier corrections, none of which this command overwrites. The sync-conflict-rename and manual-deletion premises are asserted by the candidate, not evidenced.

THE GROUNDED FAILURE: a legacy flat-format universe (root-level universe.json + vaults.json + collections.json + settings.json + workspaces.json, no `.constellation/` — the exact shape migrate_to_constellation exists for). Picking it via the third door creates `.constellation/` with a fresh empty manifest set. The loss is silent and PERMANENT: migrate_to_constellation early-returns forever after (line 367, `cdir.exists()`), and open_existing_universe now prefers the new empty `cdir/universe.json` (1220) over the root fallback (1222). Library registrations, collections, workspaces, property-types, bookmarks, the universe name/created date and every cUniverse child become unreachable, with Ok returned. No guard, no surfaced error, no self-correction — none of the refutation criteria apply.

FIX: mirror migrate_legacy_data — guard each write with `if !exists()`; call `migrate_to_constellation(library_dir)?` before the gate; and widen the gate to also refuse when root-level `universe.json`/`vaults.json` or any populated `.constellation` store is present, routing to open_existing_universe instead.

summary: `OverrideStore::save_to_path` does temp+rename with NO fsync before the rename and a FIXED temp name (`arabic-overrides.json.tmp`) — the last persisted-state writer that never adopted `universe::atomic_write`, whose doc comment (universe.rs:164-192) names both defects as the reasons it exists (PJ-140 missing fsync, PJ-187 fixed temp name).
silent_failure_scenario: The user authors Arabic tokenizer overrides in Settings (`add_arabic_override`, overrides.rs:753). `save_to_path` writes the temp and renames — but never fsyncs the temp, so on NTFS the rename can be committed while the data blocks are still unflushed. Power is lost minutes later. On reboot `<universe>/.constellation/arabic-overrides.json` exists under its final name as zeros/garbage. This file is the ONLY on-disk record of those overrides. At the next universe activation `activate_layered_for_universe` fails to parse it and universe.rs:1087-1092 catches the error, prints an `eprintln!` (invisible in a release build — there is no console) and calls `clear_active()`, installing an EMPTY store. Every subsequent FTS5 tokenization silently reverts to the un-overridden analysis: Arabic search results change, and the user is never told their overrides stopped applying. The fixed temp name additionally means a failed `fs::rename` leaves `arabic-overrides.json.tmp` behind (line 402 propagates via `?` with no cleanup), which the next writer will reuse and overwrite.
reason:
CONFIRMED on the fsync leg; the PJ-187 fixed-temp-name leg is refuted as a standalone defect.

Verified in code: `OverrideStore::save_to_path` (src-tauri/src/arabic/overrides.rs:398-403) does `serde_json::to_vec_pretty` → `std::fs::write(&tmp, &json)` → `std::fs::rename(&tmp, path)` with NO fsync anywhere. A grep of every `fs::rename` in src-tauri/src confirms this is the only persisted-STATE writer still on a bare write+rename: `universe::atomic_write` (universe.rs:186-212) does `File::create`/`write_all`/`sync_all()` before the rename and uses a per-write unique temp; `write_gate`, `link_life.rs:638` and `cece/reliability.rs:171` all fsync; the only other bare-rename sites (arabic/fst_bake.rs:354, lexicon/bake.rs:185) do best-effort `sync_all().ok()` and are rebuildable derived caches, not user-authored state. universe.rs:194-198 documents this exact requirement ("fsync BEFORE the rename — otherwise power loss can land the rename while the data blocks are still unflushed, leaving a zero-length/garbage file under the FINAL name") two files away; this site never adopted it.

Concrete reachable failure: the user authors overrides in Settings → Arabic Overrides (ArabicOverridesPanel.svelte:145 → add_arabic_override, overrides.rs:743-757). `<universe>/.constellation/arabic-overrides.json` is the SOLE on-disk record (grep confirms no second store, no export, no rebuild source — path_in_universe, overrides.rs:340-342, is the only producer/consumer). Power loss inside the unflushed window publishes zeros/garbage under the final name. At next activation, activate_layered_for_universe fails to parse; universe.rs:1087-1093 catches it, emits only an `eprintln!` (dev-only — release builds have no console, per the standing devtools rule) and calls `clear_active()`, installing an empty store. Every subsequent FTS5 tokenization silently reverts to un-overridden analysis: Arabic search results change and the user is never told at the point of effect. Unannounced, unrecoverable loss of user-authored data.

What I refuted in the candidate (and why severity is not higher): the classic compounding shape does NOT occur here. read_arabic_overrides (720-728), add_arabic_override (750-751) and remove_arabic_override (774-775) all `map_err` the parse error into Result<_, String>, and ArabicOverridesPanel.svelte:102-104 renders `loadError` — so the corruption IS surfaced whenever the user opens that panel, and the app will never overwrite the corrupt file with an empty store (no "writes the emptiness back"). The fixed-temp-name leg is also weak on its own: this file has exactly two writers, both from the single ArabicOverridesPanel mounted once in SettingsModal.svelte:1467 in the main-window layout — no second-screen or autosave co-writer exists — and a leftover `.tmp` after a failed rename is cosmetic (the next write truncates it) while the rename error itself is returned to the UI.

Fix: replace lines 400-403 with `crate::universe::atomic_write(path, &json)` — the existing hardened helper, which closes both the fsync gap and the temp-name reuse in one line.

summary: `de_canonicalize_library` reads the `.meta.json` sidecar with `fs::read_to_string(&sc_path).ok()`, conflating a TRANSIENT read failure with 'no original filename', silently falls back to the canonical filename — and then deletes the sidecar (`let _ = fs::remove_file(&sc_path)`, line 1072), destroying the only record of the original name while counting the file as `restored`.
silent_failure_scenario: A library contains `20260410T153045Z_IMG_E5F6.png` plus `20260410T153045Z_IMG_E5F6.png.meta.json` whose `original_filename` is `Family Photo 2019.png`. The user de-canonicalizes the library (`de_canonicalize_library`, registered at lib.rs:714 and exposed by `deCanonicalizeLibrary` in src/lib/importers/store.ts:76). While the walk runs, OneDrive or Defender holds the sidecar open for a moment — the everyday Windows sharing violation that `universe::read_persisted_json` (universe.rs:265-270) exists specifically to distinguish. Line 1058's `.ok()` collapses that error to `None`, `unwrap_or_else` at line 1061 substitutes the CANONICAL filename as the 'original', the file is renamed to itself, and line 1072 then deletes the sidecar unconditionally. `result.restored += 1` — no entry is pushed to `result.errors`, so the UI reports full success. The original human filename is permanently gone with no error anywhere. (Currently latent: the wrapper is exported but no UI button calls it yet — one wire-up away from live.)
reason: Verified against the real code. canonical.rs:1057 uses `fs::read_to_string(&sc_path).ok()`, collapsing a transient/permission/sharing-violation read error into `None`; `unwrap_or_else` (1060) then substitutes the CANONICAL filename as the 'original', and line 1073 unconditionally deletes the sidecar (`let _ = fs::remove_file`) while line 1074 counts `restored += 1` with nothing pushed to `result.errors`. The codebase's own `universe.rs:263-274` (`read_persisted_json`) exists specifically to forbid this conflation ("Permission-denied, sharing violations (the Windows AV/sync case) and I/O errors all mean the data is there and unread"), so the correct pattern is present in-tree and simply not used here. REACHABILITY — the candidate's "latent, no UI button" caveat is WRONG in the app's favour of confirming: canonical.rs:1445 calls `de_canonicalize_library` from `repair_external_libraries_on_startup`, which `src/routes/+layout.svelte:3431` fires AUTOMATICALLY at boot behind a one-shot `localStorage` flag (`constellation:canonical-repair-done`) — a flag this project has already proven non-durable, so it can re-fire. SILENCE — that command returns only `Vec<String>` of library names; `result.errors` is `eprintln!`-ed (1448) and discarded, the frontend only `console.log`s, and devtools is dev-only in release builds, so no error can reach the user on this path even if one were pushed. DAMAGE IS WORSE THAN CLAIMED — with `orig` = the canonical filename, `unique_path` (1173-1185) finds that name occupied by the file itself and returns `...E5F6 (1).png`; `gate_rename`'s dest-exists guard (write_gate.rs:600) does not fire because that path is free, so the attachment is renamed to a mangled THIRD name (breaking `![[20260410T153045Z_IMG_E5F6.png]]` embeds) and only then is the sidecar — the sole on-disk record of `Family Photo 2019.png` — deleted. PRECONDITIONS ARE REAL: importers.rs:930-941 writes the `.meta.json` sidecar for non-markdown imports, `is_canonical_filename` matches the `.png` while the `.meta.json` is correctly excluded at line 1003, and the `library_has_canonical_md` gate (1440) is satisfied by .md files from the same legacy import. NO SELF-CORRECTION: the mangled stem still satisfies `is_canonical_filename`, so a re-run appends another ` (1)`. Every refutation route was tried and failed — the write is not durable-and-checked, the error is surfaced nowhere, no guard/gate/trigger intervenes, and the path is reached without user action.

summary: The right-sidebar Tasks panel's `onToggle` swallows a failed task toggle into `console.error` and never restores the checkbox, so the box stays ticked while the note's `.md` is unchanged — the exact defect PJ-187 fixed in GlobalTasksView and PJ-207 §15 assumed was fixed in all three callers.
silent_failure_scenario: The note open in the editor has unsaved keystrokes and its file is momentarily locked (AV scan / Syncthing / OneDrive). Because the throw skipped lines 9739-9744, `sidebarTasks` is never reassigned, and the `$effect` that populates it (+layout.svelte:2042-2058) only re-runs on a sidebar-tab or note change — so Svelte never re-applies `checked` and the tick persists for the rest of the session. Release builds have devtools disabled, so `console.error` is invisible. The user reads the panel as 'done', closes the note, and the task silently remains open on disk. store.ts:1398-1403's own comment asserts 'All three callers already have a failure path — this is what makes them run'; that claim is false for this mount and for the Calendar mount.
reason: Real, reachable, silent false-success at src/routes/+layout.svelte:9745. Verified in code: (1) the sidebar mount passes no `readOnly` and TasksPanel.svelte:20 defaults it false, so the checkbox is live; (2) TasksPanel.svelte:136-142 renders `checked={task.completed}` one-way with an `onToggle(filePath, lineNumber)` signature that carries no element handle, so the host cannot restore the box — and I compiled that snippet against the installed Svelte 5.53.7, which emits `$.set_checked`, whose guard at node_modules/svelte/src/internal/client/dom/elements/attributes.js:105-113 early-returns on an unchanged value, so even a rescan will not un-tick it (only destroying the keyed block does); (3) the handler's only failure path is a bare `console.error`, invisible in release builds. The invoke rejects, toggleTaskReconciled throws, and the box stays ticked while `- [ ]` is untouched on disk with nothing surfaced. Partial refutation, applied to severity: the dirty-note `write_failed` branch IS surfaced via standardSaveEnv's onError → reportSaveFailure (store.ts:500) save-health banner; `path_mismatch` is unreachable because flushIfDirty passes the model's own m.path as expectPath; and "persists for the rest of the session" is overstated — the stale tick clears on note/sidebar-tab switch when the keyed each-block is re-created. No source-of-truth loss or corruption occurs: the .md stays correct and the divergence is display-only, so this is a bounded false-success, not an app-killer.

summary: `handleSave`'s `if (saving) return;` DROPS a save request outright while a previous disk write is in flight — but NotePane has already cleared `dirty` at save-REQUEST time (NotePane.svelte:362) and never restores it, so the dropped save is never re-attempted and the note reports itself saved while the disk stays stale.
silent_failure_scenario: Note open in NotePane on a slow/AV-scanned/network path. User types → `dirty = true`, debounce armed (NotePane.svelte:595). At 1500 ms `doSave()` runs: it sets `dirty = false` FIRST (NotePane.svelte:361-362), then calls `onsave` → `handleSave` sets `saving = true` and awaits `saveNoteSession` (the write goes through gate_write's fsync plus an up-to-5-attempt sharing-violation retry with 50/100/150/200 ms backoff — seconds are reachable). The user keeps typing during that window; the debounce re-arms and fires a second `doSave()`, which again clears `dirty` and calls `handleSave` — where `if (saving) return;` discards it before `editBody`, before `markRecentWrite`, and before `saveNoteSession`. When the first write settles, `.finally(() => saving = false)` runs but nothing re-arms: `dirty` is already false, so the 30 s idle timer's `doSave()` (NotePane.svelte:1015 → 361) returns immediately, and the teardown `doFlush()` passes `dirty` as `needsDiskSave = false`, so the teardown takes the no-disk-write branch (NoteEditor.svelte:367-392) and only stashes the write-ahead net. The model is genuinely dirty and holds the text (onDocChange keeps it current at :770), yet no disk write is scheduled, no save-health failure is recorded, and no unsaved state is shown — the note sits stale on disk for the rest of the session unless the user types again or the tab is torn down. The guard is also redundant now: noteSession.save already serialises concurrent same-id saves through `saveChains` (noteSession.ts:200-239) precisely so the newest content writes last, so chaining is available where this drops.

summary: saveTabContent's `if (saveLocks.get(tabId)) return;` drops a property save whose write-lock is held by an in-flight save; the edit is left only in the dirty model with no scheduled write, while the in-flight save's compare-and-clear wipes the net.

The user changes a property in the Properties panel (or adds a tag, or promotes a stage). saveTabContent pushes the change into the model at line 1784 — correct, the model is now dirty at V2 — then hits line 1805 and returns. The comment there ("a write is already in flight; the model has this edit") is true but incomplete: no code path re-drives the write. The debounce belongs to NotePane's `docChanged` listener and a frontmatter-only edit never touches the CM6 doc, so it never arms; the idle timer gates on NotePane's `dirty`, which a property edit never sets. When the in-flight V1 write lands, `clearWriteAheadIf(path, contentV1)` (store.ts:382) matches and clears the net. The property now exists only in the in-memory model: the panel shows it, disk does not have it, the net does not have it, note_meta does not have it (no reindex ran), and no banner exists. It is persisted only if the user later edits the body, switches tabs, or closes the app cleanly (flushOutgoing / flushAllForAppClose); a crash before any of those loses the property change silently.
reason: Mechanism verified in code, but the candidate's trigger is wrong and the impact is smaller than claimed. saveLocks is set ONLY by saveTabContent itself (store.ts:1806 — grep shows no other setter); body autosaves go through saveNoteSession directly (NoteEditor.svelte:260/298/399/547) and never take the lock, so the described "body autosave in flight" cannot cause the drop. The reachable trigger is two frontmatter-writing actions on the SAME tab overlapping one in-flight gated write — e.g. a PropertyEditor commit whose atomic_write enters the AV/sharing-violation retry ladder (write_gate.rs:281-285, ~500 ms of sleeps and still succeeding) while the user adds a tag (+layout.svelte:7005 addTagToNote) or connects a link (store.ts:1498). In that window: store.ts:1784 puts the edit in the model, store.ts:1805 returns silently, saveTabContent returns void so addTagToNote cannot see the drop (its own 2026-08-01 inspection comment enumerates three visible drop-exits; this is an uncovered fourth), and no reindex runs (runPostSave is past the guard) so the tag/property is absent from note_meta/FTS. When write #1 lands, noteModel.ts:509 markSaved only advances savedVersion so the model stays dirty at V2 (edit retained), while clearWriteAheadIf(path, contentV1) (store.ts:382) matches the net set before the await (noteSession.ts:250) and deterministically WIPES it — nothing re-nets on a props-only model edit (noteSession.ts:106-144). No re-drive exists: NotePane doSave gates on the local `dirty` set only in the docChanged listener (NotePane.svelte:360/586), so the 30 s idle timer no-ops for a frontmatter-only edit; the ~10 s auto-retry (+layout.svelte:1746-1748) iterates saveHealth, which is empty because the write SUCCEEDED; PropertyEditor re-seeds seededRows from the model (line 1022) before the dropped call and never retries. Net result: a dirty model with no crash net, no scheduled write, and a stale index, with zero surfaced signal. Downgraded from MED to LOW because it is not loss of durable data — the model keeps the edit, the panel shows it, and every departure path persists it (flushOpenTabOrAbort, nav flush, flushAllForAppClose, PJ-103 app-close flush); actual loss requires an additional hard crash inside the window, and short of that the damage is an unbounded but self-healing disk/index divergence.

summary: `withAutoUpdatedDate` is applied to the rows handed to `plan`, but `touched` is computed from the PRE-transform rows, so `plan`'s touched-gate drops the refreshed `updated:`/`modified:` date on every Properties-panel save once that key already exists.
silent_failure_scenario: REPRODUCED: with seeded/local rows `[{updated,2020-01-01,date},{stage,…}]` and the user editing only `stage`, `touchedSince` returns `{'stage'}`; `plan(withAutoUpdatedDate(local), model, seededKeys, touched)` emits ONLY `set stage`, because the `updated` row hits `if (touchedKeys && !touchedKeys.has(row.key)) continue` at propsCommit.ts:117. The whole point of extracting `withAutoUpdatedDate` (store.ts:1742-1745) was that “the intent commit path applies exactly the same rule as the legacy whole-array path”, and on this path it never applies at all. Consequence: a note edited through the Properties panel keeps advertising a stale `updated:` date in its own frontmatter forever (the key is only ever refreshed if it does NOT yet exist, where `plan` emits an ungated `add`, or via `addTagToNote`, which still goes through `saveTabContent`'s whole-array branch). Every derived surface that reads `updated` — Bases columns, sorts, review scheduling heuristics — inherits the wrong date, with nothing to indicate it.
reason: Real, reachable, silent — and reproduced by running the actual planner. PropertyEditor.svelte:989 computes `touched = touchedSince(seededRows, editableProps)` from the PRE-transform rows, then line 990 hands `withAutoUpdatedDate(editableProps)` to `plan`. The refreshed `updated`/`modified` row is therefore never in `touchedKeys`, and propsCommit.ts:117 (`if (touchedKeys && !touchedKeys.has(row.key)) continue`) drops it before the diff. Verified with vitest against the real `plan`/`touchedSince`/`withAutoUpdatedDate`: model `[updated:2020-01-01(date), stage:seed]`, user edits only `stage` → `touched=['stage']`, `ops=[{"op":"set","key":"stage",...}]` — the date op is absent. With `updated` absent from the model the ungated `add` branch fires and emits today's date, which is why the defect only bites once the key exists. The path is live (`ownershipFlag.ts:33 PROPS_SINGLE_OWNERSHIP = true`) and the legacy application is bypassed because `commitAndSave` passes `propsAlreadyInModel: true` (PropertyEditor.svelte:1023 → store.ts:1784 skips `editNoteProps(withAutoUpdatedDate(...))`). Nothing surfaces it: `changed` is true from the real edit and `refused` is empty, so the save reports success; the panel re-seeds from the model, which still holds the stale date, so it never self-corrects. The in-code contract at store.ts:1743-1745 ("so the intent commit path applies exactly the same rule as the legacy whole-array path") is falsified — on that path it applies never. Refutation levers checked and rejected: no guard/version-gate/trigger intervenes, the path is the ordinary Properties-panel edit, and no error is raised anywhere. Severity held at LOW, not raised: no user-authored content is lost or corrupted, and disk/model/panel/index all agree on the same (stale) value — there is no source-of-truth-vs-index divergence. It is also not the sole cause of stale dates: `composeModel` (noteModel.ts:161) applies no auto-date either, so body-only edits never refreshed `updated`; the rule survives only on the three whole-array `saveTabContent` callers (addTagToNote at +layout.svelte:7005, addLinkToNote at store.ts:1498, and the legacy fallbacks at PropertyEditor.svelte:984/988). Fix is one line — compute `plan`'s input once and derive `touched` from the same transformed array (or exempt the auto-date keys from the touched-gate).

summary: `migrateLocalStorage` invokes `save_universe_bookmarks`, a Tauri command that does not exist anywhere in `src-tauri/src` — so the bookmarks leg of the first-run migration always fails into its `catch`, leaving the user's bookmarks only in localStorage, which PJ-110 proved is non-durable.
silent_failure_scenario: A legacy user runs the first-run Universe setup. `migrateLocalStorage` (UniverseSetup.svelte:234) moves settings, workspaces and property types into the Universe, then at line 251 calls `invoke('save_universe_bookmarks', { bookmarks })`. No such command is registered (a whole-tree grep of `src-tauri/src` returns nothing; only `read_universe_bookmarks` exists), so Tauri rejects with 'command not found', the `catch` at line 253 logs to a console the release build does not have, and `constellation-bookmarks` is correctly kept out of `migrated`. The result: `bookmarks.json` is never written, so the one-time Bookmarks→Starred adoption that `loadCollections` performs (it reads `read_universe_bookmarks`) finds an empty file forever, and the user's bookmarks remain solely in localStorage — the store PJ-110 demonstrated can be wiped wholesale by a leveldb log-orphan. Nothing user-visible ever reports that the migration leg did not run; the setup completes normally and the bookmarks quietly never appear as Starred items.
reason: Verified in source: `save_universe_bookmarks` does not exist. src-tauri/src/lib.rs:661 registers only `universe::read_universe_bookmarks`, and a whole-tree grep of every .rs for \"bookmarks\" finds no save-side command; universe.rs:1651-1653 states it outright (\"MIG-092: READ-ONLY now… nothing writes bookmarks.json anymore\"). So `invoke('save_universe_bookmarks', { bookmarks })` at UniverseSetup.svelte:251 is rejected by Tauri 100% of the time, not intermittently. Every refutation route fails: (1) Not surfaced — the catch at line 254 does console.error only; the wizard's `error` $state is never set, `creating` clears, `step = 2`, setup completes normally, and per project rule devtools is dev-only so a release user sees nothing. (2) Reachable — check_migration_needed (universe.rs:1404-1415) returns true when universes.json is absent and legacy vaults.json exists; handleNext (lines 107-110) then runs migrateLegacyData followed by migrateLocalStorage. (3) No self-correction — a grep of all of src for 'constellation-bookmarks' returns ONLY the three lines inside UniverseSetup.svelte; no other code path ever reads that localStorage key, so the surviving copy is orphaned, not preserved, and PJ-110 proved that store is non-durable. (4) The destination never gets the data another way — migrate_legacy_data (universe.rs:1941-1943) writes bookmarks.json as \"[]\", and loadCollections (src/lib/libraries/store.ts:2204-2219) runs the ONE-TIME CL.migrateBookmarks seed against read_universe_bookmarks, gets the empty array, then `if (r.migrated) void saveCollections()` persists the result so the adoption never re-runs — the single migration slot is consumed against empty input, permanently. (5) The PJ-207 §15 guard correctly keeps the key out of `migrated` so it is not deleted, but that preserves bytes in a store nothing can read — deferred loss, not recovery. Net: a legacy user's bookmarks are silently and permanently never adopted as Starred items, with no signal at any point. Severity held at LOW rather than higher because the lost object is curation metadata (favorited paths), not note content — the .md source of truth is untouched — and the population is limited to pre-universe legacy installs passing through the first-run wizard; it is not NONE because the loss is permanent, silent, and not reconstructible by the user. Related dead code carrying the same broken command: src/lib/universe/store.ts:109-111 (`saveUniverseBookmarks`, zero callers).

summary: `content_type_set_manual` writes the frontmatter and the `note_meta.content_type` mirror but never calls `clear_suggestions`, while its horizontal twin `sources_set_manual` does (line 785). A vertical-axis resolution whose horizontal axis has no settled primary therefore leaves the `sources_suggestions` row alive while the UI has already dropped the card.
