The user picks a vertical chip. `cece_resolve_disambiguation` takes the `other_axis_still_split == false` branch, calls `content_type_set_manual` (which does not clear the row), finds `other_axis_settled == None` so the `sources_set_manual` co-write that WOULD have cleared it never runs, and returns Ok(None). The frontend does `queue = queue.filter(...)` and the card vanishes — but the row is still in `sources_suggestions`. Two silent consequences: the card reappears in the Cataloger's universe queue on the next `sources_list_pending_suggestions`, and `enumerate_pending` (classifier/scan_job.rs:268) excludes every note that has a suggestion row, so the background scan will never revisit that note again for as long as the stale row survives. No error is raised on either side.
reason: Verified in source. `content_type_set_manual` (sources/mod.rs:1254-1258) omits the `clear_suggestions` its horizontal twin performs (mod.rs:785). In `cece_resolve_disambiguation` (classifier/mod.rs:371-459) the vertical branch calls it, and the only compensating clear — the co-write `sources_set_manual` at :434-437 — is gated on `other_axis_settled`, which `extract_other_axis_settled` (:512-537) returns None for whenever horizontal's `primary` is absent/null/empty. Synthesis produces exactly that state at cece/synthesis.rs:266-277 (no cataloger voiced that axis → primary None, regime Unanimous, needs_disambiguation None), and catalogers voice vertical-only by construction (structural.rs:98 abstains only when both axis hit-sets are empty; it has a dedicated `structural.vertical_only` variant), with semantic/graph/user_authority/reasoning all abstaining in a cold-start Library — the exact condition the scan job runs under. Concrete failure: card is Split on vertical only, user picks a vertical chip, the command returns Ok(None), the frontend filters the card out (SourceReviewPanel.svelte:593) with no error — a false-success — but the `sources_suggestions` row survives. `sources_list_pending_suggestions` (mod.rs:882-895) queries the table unfiltered, so the card returns on the next load with the same chips, and re-picking re-runs the identical path, so the affordance can never clear it; meanwhile `enumerate_pending` (classifier/scan_job.rs:268-271) has `WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM sources_suggestions ...)`, silently excluding the note from every future background scan while the row lives. Grep confirms no reconcile or repair prunes orphan rows (the only DELETEs are clear_suggestions, rename, reject-all, note-delete). Held to LOW rather than higher: no .md content is lost or corrupted — the pick is written to frontmatter via gate_rmw and the note_meta mirror matches; the divergence is confined to a derived queue table; the main symptom is user-visible; and Reject, Reject-all, Approve-all, and re-classification all clear the row. The Accept path is unaffected (it always invokes sources_set_manual first, even with an empty array). Fix is the one-line parity: add clear_suggestions to content_type_set_manual's DB block.

summary: The bulk semantic indexer substitutes `content: ''` when `read_note` fails and hands that to `embedNotes`, permanently storing a title-only vector in `note_embeddings` that no later run will ever replace.
silent_failure_scenario: With `enabledFeatures.semanticSearch` on, the boot `$effect` (+layout.svelte:6227-6242) fires `startSemanticIndexing()` over all ~7,800 notes in chunks of 50. For any note whose `read_note` rejects transiently — an AV scan holding the handle, a Syncthing/OneDrive placeholder not yet hydrated, a sharing violation — line 6260's `catch { return { path: n.path, name: n.name, content: '' }; }` returns an entry with EMPTY body instead of dropping it from the batch. `embedNotes` (store.ts:4232-4234) invokes `constellation_embed_notes` WITHOUT `force`, so Rust takes the non-force branch (embeddings.rs:446-456) and, seeing no existing row, proceeds to embed `format!("passage: {} {}", name, "")` (embeddings.rs:460) and `INSERT OR REPLACE INTO note_embeddings` (embeddings.rs:468-471). The write SUCCEEDS, so `count` increments and nothing anywhere reports a problem. From that moment the note has a title-only vector: `constellation_search_similar` and the semantic search tier return it for the wrong neighbours and omit it for the right ones. Every subsequent bulk run short-circuits on `existing → count += 1; continue` (embeddings.rs:456), and the boot trigger itself is gated on `status.embedded_count < allNotes.length`, which the bogus row satisfies — so the note is never re-read. Only an explicit edit (which uses `force: true` at NoteEditor.svelte:307/408) can heal it; a note the user never edits again stays silently wrong forever. `note_embeddings` is named in the brief's source-of-truth list and there is no reconcile pass for it.
reason: Mechanism verified end-to-end in source. +layout.svelte:6255-6261 keeps a note in the embed batch with content:'' when read_note rejects, silently (no log, no counter). embedNotes (store.ts:4232) omits `force`, so embeddings.rs:446-456 takes the non-force branch, finds no existing row, embeds `passage: {name} ` (line 460) and INSERT OR REPLACEs (468-471), returning Ok with count incremented — no error surfaced at any layer (the only error surface in the path is an eprintln! on inference failure). The row is then permanent: note_embeddings has no content hash/mtime/freshness column (search.rs:4700-4705 + cid_cn), every later bulk run short-circuits on `if existing { count += 1; continue; }`, and the boot gate `status.embedded_count < allNotes.length` (+layout.svelte:6235, backed by a plain SELECT COUNT(*) at embeddings.rs:497) is satisfied by the bogus row. No rebuild command exists; the only three force:true sites (NoteEditor.svelte:309/410, store.ts:650) are user saves, and reconcile.rs::relocate_row / libraries.rs:1384-1388 only repath embedding rows — nothing revalidates content. So the divergence is real, silent, and self-perpetuating. Downgraded MED -> LOW because: enabledFeatures.semanticSearch defaults false (store.ts:6793), so the path requires an opt-in plugin; note_embeddings is a purely derived index with the .md untouched and the vector recomputable (unlike the note_links earned data); federation is not a trigger (load_all_libraries -> resolve_universe_libraries covers cUniverse paths, so validate_path_in_any_library does not reject federated notes); and the most deterministic trigger — a stale note_meta row for a vanished file, since allNotes comes from note_meta (cache.rs:1249-1256) — yields a phantom row that the delete/rename/reconcile paths do clean up, leaving only the file-exists-but-read-failed case (lock/permission/non-UTF-8) as persistent. Impact is degraded relevance in an optional semantic tier for one note, not knowledge loss and not a freeze/leak. Fix is one line: drop the failed entry from the batch instead of substituting ''.

summary: Batch delete records per-item failures to `console.error` only, while its sibling batch move (fixed by the 2026-08-01 inspection) surfaces exactly the same condition in `templateActionError` — the Whole-Ecosystem half of that fix was never applied here.
silent_failure_scenario: User multi-selects 40 items in the file tree and confirms the batch delete. The loop at +layout.svelte:7145-7147 calls `deleteWithSetting(p)` per item; three throw (a note open in another program, a folder holding a locked file, a permission error on a synced subtree). Each is caught by `catch (e) { console.error('[batch delete] failed for', p, e); }` and the loop continues. Line 7148 then runs `refreshAllLoadedTrees()` and 7150 clears the selection, so the confirmation UI completes exactly as it does on full success — no count, no list, no error surface, and (release build) no console. The three survivors are re-rendered somewhere in a 40-row tree the user has just stopped looking at, indistinguishable from rows they never selected. The user believes all 40 are in the trash. The identical loop for batch MOVE two hundred lines away (+layout.svelte:6926-6936) collects `failedMoves` and raises `templateActionError` with the item names, with a comment stating the reason: 'console.error alone is invisible in a release build — the user saw N selected, some silently left behind, and no way to know which.' Batch delete was left with the pre-fix shape.
reason: Verified by reading both sites. +layout.svelte:7141-7152 (batch delete) closes the confirm dialog BEFORE the loop, catches each per-item failure with console.error only (7146), then unconditionally runs refreshAllLoadedTrees() and clearTreeSelection() — so partial failure completes byte-identically to full success, with no count, no names, no error surface, and (devtools being dev-only) no console in a release build. clearTreeSelection() even removes the highlight that would have identified the survivors, leaving them indistinguishable from rows never selected. The rejection is caught, so the global handlers at 3205-3211 never fire, and both are console.error anyway. The failure is genuinely reachable: deleteWithSetting (store.ts:4862) rethrows from resolveTrashDestination (throws at 4860 when no is_universe_notes library resolves) and from invoke('delete_path'), whose Rust side (libraries.rs:7347-7362) returns Err on validate_path_in_any_library, ensure_search_db_ready, !target.exists(), and the fs op itself (Windows sharing violation, ACL on a synced subtree). The sibling batch move at 6926-6933 raises exactly this condition into templateActionError using failedMoves + failedList() + tOr(), with a comment stating the reason; templateActionError already renders as a dismissible bar at 7654-7657 and the helpers exist at 635-645 — the surface is available and simply unwired at the delete site, so the Whole-Ecosystem half of the 2026-08-01 fix was never applied. Secondary divergence at the same site: an item whose deletePath succeeded but that throws in a later step of deleteWithSetting is never pushed to deleted[], so emitNoteDeleted (7151) is skipped for a file that IS gone (not traced to a concrete throw, so not the basis of the verdict). Severity held at LOW because the data direction is fail-safe — nothing is lost or corrupted, the files survive and remain visible in the tree; the defect is false-success on a destructive-intent action with no surfaced error. Note the single-item path at 7169-7171 has the same console-only catch, so the fix must cover both branches.
